dimensions.assessment: Affects telecommunications companies applying for high-cost universal service program funding.
dimensions.evidence: applicants for, and other recipients of, a new covered funding award

dimensions.assessment: Applicants face new technical and financial vetting requirements, with mandatory financial penalties of at least $9,000 per violation for pre-authorization defaults.
dimensions.evidence: set a penalty for pre-authorization defaults of at least $9,000 per violation

dimensions.assessment: Establishes financial penalties for defaults, but does not allocate new federal spending amounts.
dimensions.evidence: set a penalty for pre-authorization defaults of at least $9,000 per violation

dimensions.assessment: Requires the FCC to conduct a rulemaking proceeding and establish a specific vetting process for broadband funding applicants.
dimensions.evidence: the Commission shall initiate a rulemaking proceeding to establish a vetting process

dimensions.assessment: Amends permanent statute (the Communications Act of 1934) to add ongoing vetting requirements for new funding awards.
dimensions.evidence: Section 254 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 254) is amended

missing_information: The exact number of broadband funding applicants or companies that will apply for future high-cost universal service funds is not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill creates an administrative vetting process for high-cost universal service broadband funding applicants, impacting telecommunications companies applying for future awards and potentially penalizing defaults.
